title: The Coffee Tradition in Xilitla: From the Plant to Your Cup
metaTitle: Xilitla Coffee: Farm Tours and the Coffee Fair (2026)
metaDescription: Discover Xilitla's high-altitude coffee in 2026: coffee farm tours, the Coffee Fair, real prices and how to experience this tradition in the Huasteca Potosina.
excerpt: Xilitla's high-altitude coffee grows at 800 to 1,400 meters in the misty Sierra Madre Oriental. Here's how to tour the coffee farms, when the Coffee Fair happens and how to ship coffee home.
contentHtml:
Xilitla's high-altitude coffee isn't an attraction with a ticket or a museum with fixed hours: it's a living experience that starts on the misty slopes of the Sierra Madre Oriental and ends in the cup you're holding, in front of a landscape few regions of Mexico can match. The coffee farms here grow between 800 and 1,400 meters above sea level, in a cool, humid microclimate that produces beans with a complex flavor, chocolatey notes and a light fruity acidity. If you've ever wondered why the high-altitude coffee of the Huasteca Potosina has a reputation that grows year after year, the answer starts in the soil.

Planning a visit to Xilitla's coffee farms takes concrete information: which tours exist, when the Coffee Fair takes place, what other local products you can take home and how to combine it all with the nearby sights of the Huasteca Potosina. This guide brings together up-to-date information for 2026, from tour prices to the events calendar, so you can plan your trip without surprises.

At huasteca-potosina.com we work with local guides and operators in the region. This guide is updated with real experiences from people who travel the Huasteca Potosina every week. If you want to plan a full trip through the sierra, book your guided tour in the Huasteca Potosina using our suggested routes before you book any tour.

Xilitla coffee farm tours: what they include and how much they cost

Tours from Ciudad Valles: price and what to expect

The most practical way to reach the coffee farms without logistical headaches is a guided trip: our Coffee Trail (Travesía del Café) rides up by RZR (an off-road side-by-side) to a coffee farm in the sierra, with pickup from your lodging in Xilitla. It lasts about 4 hours, so you'll have the rest of the day for other spots in Xilitla, like Edward James's famous Surrealist Garden. The Coffee Trail costs $900 MXN per person and includes the guided walk through the coffee farm and a tasting of freshly roasted coffee. This kind of tour is ideal if it's your first time in the area and you'd rather not drive the mountain roads. Check availability and dates in our tours section before your trip.

Coffee shipped to your door: take the flavor home

Not everyone can travel to Xilitla, but anyone can enjoy its high-altitude coffee. Several local cooperatives and growers ship anywhere in Mexico at a flat rate of $149 MXN per package, no matter the destination. This option also works for people who have visited the region and want to keep drinking one of the most iconic local products of the Huasteca sierra. The coffee is sold roasted, as whole beans or ground, with labels that show the growing altitude and the flavor profile. If you want to try it before you buy, head up to the coffee farms on the Coffee Trail, which ends with a tasting of freshly roasted coffee.

When to visit: the Coffee Fair and Xilitla's cultural life

Xilitla Coffee Fair: August 27 to September 1

The time of year when Xilitla shows off its whole coffee-growing identity is the Coffee Fair (Feria del Café), held from August 27 to September 1. During those days, the town fills with aromas and flavors in honor of its high-altitude coffee: tastings, artisanal barista competitions, direct sales from growers and live son huasteco music, the rhythm that accompanies celebrations in the sierra. If you can pick only one time to visit Xilitla, this week offers the most complete taste of local culture. Plan your stay early, because lodging sells out fast; find options in our tours and packages section.

The Sunday Huapangueada: music and tradition every week

If your visit doesn't line up with the August fair, Xilitla has a standing cultural date every Sunday: the Huapangueada Dominical, held in the Main Square from 2 to 5 p.m. Huapango (the region's traditional son music) is the perfect soundtrack for an afternoon with a coffee in hand, surrounded by the town's colonial architecture and the year-round green of the sierra. It's free and open to any traveler who shows up on their own. Paired with a visit to the local markets that sell local products like coffee, piloncillo (unrefined cane sugar) and Teenek textiles, it makes for a Sunday unlike any other in the Huasteca Potosina.

Practical tips for visiting the coffee farms in 2026

Best time: October through February is coffee harvest season. Visiting during that period lets you see the whole process, from picking the red coffee cherries to wet processing. The rainy season (June–September) makes the coffee farms even greener, but the mountain roads can get tricky.

Getting to Xilitla: From Ciudad Valles it's an hour and a half by road. You can take public transportation with a connection in Aquismón or book a tour from the city. Check route options on Google Maps before you head out.

What else to see in the area: Xilitla is just the start of the Huasteca Potosina. From here you can extend your trip to the pools of Tamasopo or Tamul Waterfall. Find more guides to the region:

  • Complete guide to the Tamasopo pools 2026
  • How to get to Tamul Waterfall from Ciudad Valles
  • Edward James's Surrealist Garden: what to know before you go

Buy responsibly: When you buy high-altitude coffee directly from local cooperatives or at the Coffee Fair, you support grower families in the sierra who work with traditional, sustainable methods. Always ask about the origin and growing altitude; those details guarantee you're taking home an authentic product of the Huasteca Potosina.

Frequently asked questions about high-altitude coffee

What makes Xilitla's high-altitude coffee different from other Mexican coffees?

Xilitla's high-altitude coffee grows between 800 and 1,400 meters above sea level, in a humid microclimate in the Sierra Madre Oriental. That altitude slows down the ripening of the bean, concentrating sugars and producing a more complex flavor profile, with chocolatey notes and a soft fruity acidity.

Can I visit a coffee farm without booking an organized tour?

Yes, you can get to Xilitla on your own and contact local growers or cooperatives directly. However, a guided trip makes it easier to get into the farms and gives you context for the whole process: the Coffee Trail costs $900 MXN per person. We pick you up at your lodging in Xilitla, by RZR, between 8:00 and 9:00 a.m. From Ciudad Valles, the transfer costs extra: we'll send you a quote on WhatsApp.

When is the 2026 Xilitla Coffee Fair?

The Xilitla Coffee Fair usually runs from August 27 to September 1. During that week there are tastings, direct sales of local products, son huasteco music and cultural activities. We recommend booking lodging early, since demand goes up considerably.

Can I buy high-altitude coffee to ship home if I can't travel?

Yes. Several growers and cooperatives in Xilitla ship anywhere in Mexico at a flat rate of $149 MXN per package, no matter the destination. The coffee ships roasted, as whole beans or ground. It's a great way to support local growers without having to travel to the Huasteca sierra.
